title: Linear orders of successor Scott sentence complexities exist in all three complexity classes
source_title: Scott sentence complexities of linear orderings

standard_prerequisites.name: Successor complexity classes
standard_prerequisites.statement: S_infinity, dS_infinity and P_infinity denote the successive classes of Scott sentence complexity, and complexity is the least rank at which a Scott sentence exists.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the three families of complexities realised.

standard_prerequisites.name: Multiplication of orders by Z to the alpha
standard_prerequisites.statement: For an order L the order Z^alpha times L has the back-and-forth relations obtained from those of L by shifting by twice alpha.
standard_prerequisites.use: It shifts the known examples of complexity S_infinity 4 and 5 to every successor rank.

standard_prerequisites.name: Back-and-forth analysis of well-orderings
standard_prerequisites.statement: The back-and-forth relations of well-orderings are known and give the optimality of the Scott sentence complexities of omega to the alpha and of omega to the alpha times two.
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the two base families with odd successor ranks.

core_obligations: Realise every complexity of the form S_infinity alpha plus n with n at least 4 by taking the orders Z^alpha times L_4 and Z^alpha times L_5, using the known lower bound Z^alpha times L_4 <= Z^alpha times K_4 at rank 2 alpha plus 4 (source lines 1371-1377).

Realise the dS_infinity family from the order Q plus 2 plus Q at rank 2, shifted by Z^alpha, and use the analysis of well-orderings for omega^alpha times 2 to reach every successor rank (source lines 1379-1385).
Realise the P_infinity family from Q at rank 2 and from omega^alpha, again shifted by Z^alpha (source lines 1387-1391).

proof_roadmap.step: S_infinity family from the rank four and five examples and their lower bounds.
dS_infinity family from Q plus 2 plus Q and the well-ordering analysis.
P_infinity family from Q and from omega to the alpha.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled corollary at source0.tex lines 1361-1368: there are linear orders of Scott sentence complexity S_infinity(alpha plus n) for every countable alpha and n at least 4, of complexity dS_infinity(alpha plus n) for n at least 1, and of complexity P_infinity(alpha plus n) for n at least 1. The statement lists nine families and gives no examples, and the proof (source lines 1370-1392) has to produce each family by combining a base example with the shift by Z^alpha, and in each case the optimality of the resulting rank must be secured: for the first family by the ranked lower bound between the order and its companion, for the second and third by the known back-and-forth analysis of well-orderings, which the author invokes for omega^alpha times two and for omega^alpha. Which base example produces which successor rank, and where the optimality comes from in each of the three classes, is exactly what the statement omits.
